labels.label: bzdef:c2s1d1_poche_affine

hypotheses.paper: V une variété localement affine de dimension n
hypotheses.note: any ChartedSpace (Fin n → ℝ) V; connected/Hausdorff/countable (plan F6) never used; HasGroupoid only in the theorems that use it

hypotheses.paper: un ouvert connexe P de V
hypotheses.note: fields isOpen, isConnected (Mathlib's IsConnected is nonempty; nonemptiness is forced anyway by condition a's IsGLB)

hypotheses.paper: une carte φ de P dans ℝⁿ compatible avec la structure affine
hypotheses.note: φ : OpenPartialHomeomorph with φ.source = P and IsCompatibleChart (GAR n) φ (Ch. 1, Déf. 13); reading « carte » = injective, see questions

hypotheses.paper: une fonction linéaire z sur ℝⁿ appelée cote
hypotheses.note: reading: z : (Fin n → ℝ) →ᵃ[ℝ] ℝ, an affine function (Ch. 1, Déf. 2, Exemple), see questions

hypotheses.paper: a. sur φ(P), z a pour borne inférieure 0 et est majorée par 1
hypotheses.note: IsGLB (z '' (φ '' P)) 0 and z (φ x) ≤ 1 for x ∈ P

hypotheses.paper: b. (M, N) un segment de V, M ∈ P; φ̃ une carte compatible d'un voisinage de (M, N) ayant en M même germe que φ; si z(φ̃(N)) < 1, N ∈ P
hypotheses.note: for EVERY such φ̃ (IsAffSegment = Ch. 1, Déf. 14; Sg ⊆ φ̃.source; φ̃ =ᶠ[𝓝 M] φ); proved equivalent to « for SOME such φ̃ », and such φ̃ always exist (IsAffSegment.forall_chart_iff_exists)

findings: About the two UNLABELLED examples (l.155–179), not about the definitions: with « carte » an injective chart (the paper's convention: l.559–562, l.723, l.552, l.572–573; Ch. 1, Déf. 13), the conclusion « le triple (P, p, z) définit une poche de W » (l.160, resp. l.176–178) needs p injective on P, which the examples do not assume. Counterexample (affine case, n = 2; argued, NOT formalized): W = ℝ × ]1/10, 1/2[ with the affine structure pulled back by p(θ, r) = (1/2 + r cos θ, r sin θ) (the universal cover of the annulus 1/10 < |q − (1/2, 0)| < 1/2), z(x, y) = x; then p(W) is the annulus, 0 < z < 1 on it with infimum 0, so P = p⁻¹(z < 1) = W is connected and meets every hypothesis of the example, but p is not injective on P. Formalized with the injectivity added: Benzecri.exemple_poche_affine, Benzecri.exemple_poche_projective. Question for the author, on these unlabelled examples only: add « p injective sur P » (as formalized), or read them as describing the univalent situation that § 3, Théorème shows is always the case for a sweepable V?
questions: « fonction linéaire z sur ℝⁿ » (l.104) is read as an AFFINE function ℝⁿ → ℝ (`(Fin n → ℝ) →ᵃ[ℝ] ℝ`), the paper's own term (Ch. 1, Déf. 2, Exemple: « application affine de A dans ℝ, ou fonction linéaire sur A »), as it must be on H̊ in Déf. 1′. The homogeneous reading (z(0) = 0) gives the same pockets up to a translation of the chart φ; the affine reading is the more general.

Constant cotes are not excluded by the text: (P, φ, 0) is a pocket iff P = V (for V connected), e.g. (ℝⁿ, id, 0) (Benzecri.isPocheAff_model). Kept; a non-degenerate pocket (indeed a strict shell) is Benzecri.exists_isCoqueStricteAff_demiDroite.

« carte » = injective chart (OpenPartialHomeomorph) is the PAPER'S CONVENTION, not an open reading: Benzécri refuses the name « carte compatible » to a local homeomorphism with all its jets in J(V) until it is shown to be a global homeomorphism (l.559–562, p. 254: « φ̃ est un homéomorphisme local : il faut montrer que φ̃ est un homéomorphisme global »); § 3, Prop. 2 concludes « p est une carte de V » for a projection already compatible with the structure (l.723); Ch. 1, Prop. 2 calls the developing map « une application »; the proof of § 3, Théorème uses the injectivity (l.552, l.572–573); and Ch. 1's marked Déf. 13 and 14 are on OpenPartialHomeomorph. The mark does not rest on an unruled reading. (The only author-facing point it raises concerns the unlabelled examples: see findings.)

hypotheses.note: φ.source = P, IsCompatibleChart (GSR n) φ, field image_subset

hypotheses.paper: une fonction linéaire z sur H̊ considéré comme espace affin (Déf. 6)
hypotheses.note: z : openHemisphere l →ᵃ[ℝ] ℝ for the AddTorsor (HemiTrans l) of Déf. 6 (Hemisphere.lean)

hypotheses.paper: a. sur φ(P), borne inférieure 0, majorée par 1
hypotheses.note: on φ(P) read in H̊: IsGLB (z '' ((↑) ⁻¹' (φ '' P))) 0, z ≤ 1

hypotheses.paper: b. … Alors φ̃(M, N) ⊂ H̊ et, si z(φ̃(N)) < 1, N ∈ P
hypotheses.note: for EVERY φ̃ (equivalent to SOME, IsProjSegment.forall_chart_iff_exists); IsProjSegment = Ch. 1, Déf. 14 (closed segment of Déf. 7)

findings: The projective example (l.172–179) has the same gap as the affine one: p must be injective on P for (P, H̊, p, z) to be a pocket in the chart reading (see the finding on bzdef:c2s1d1_poche_affine); formalized with that hypothesis as Benzecri.exemple_poche_projective.
questions: [sic] l.134 (flagged l.135): « (Le système P, H̊, φ, z) » read « Le système (P, H̊, φ, z) », as the transcription's comment says; not a finding.

H̊ is carried by its equation l (unique up to a positive factor, Déf. 5) rather than as a set: for another equation c·l of the same hemisphere the cote z transports along Ch. 1's hemiTransEquiv (the affine structure of Déf. 6 does not depend on the equation); this transport is not stated here.

« fonction linéaire z, appelée cote, sur H̊ considéré comme espace affin » (l.131) is read as an AFFINE function on the affine space H̊ of Déf. 6 (`openHemisphere l →ᵃ[ℝ] ℝ`), the paper's own term (Ch. 1, Déf. 2, Exemple: « application affine de A dans ℝ, ou fonction linéaire sur A »); on an affine space no other reading exists.

« carte » = injective chart (OpenPartialHomeomorph) is the PAPER'S CONVENTION, not an open reading: Benzécri refuses the name « carte compatible » to a local homeomorphism with all its jets in J(V) until it is shown to be a global homeomorphism (l.559–562, p. 254: « φ̃ est un homéomorphisme local : il faut montrer que φ̃ est un homéomorphisme global »); § 3, Prop. 2 concludes « p est une carte de V » for a projection already compatible with the structure (l.723); Ch. 1, Prop. 2 calls the developing map « une application »; the proof of § 3, Théorème uses the injectivity (l.552, l.572–573); and Ch. 1's marked Déf. 13 and 14 are on OpenPartialHomeomorph. The mark does not rest on an unruled reading. (The only author-facing point it raises concerns the unlabelled examples: see findings.)

hypotheses.paper: V une variété localement affine de dimension n
hypotheses.note: [ChartedSpace (Fin n → ℝ) V] [HasGroupoid V (affGroupoid n)]; « variété » (plan F6) not used

hypotheses.paper: (P, φ, z) une poche de V
hypotheses.note: IsPocheAff P φ z

hypotheses.paper: j un isomorphisme compatible avec la structure affine de ℝⁿ sur un hémisphère ouvert H̊ de S(n)
hypotheses.note: j : (Fin n → ℝ) ≃ᵃ[ℝ] openHemisphere l, ANY open hemisphere (l ≠ 0); j ∘ φ is φ.trans of the open embedding y ↦ j y (isOpenEmbedding_coe_affineEquiv), z ∘ j⁻¹ is z.comp j.symm

hypotheses.paper: V considérée comme variété localement projective (Ch. 1, Déf. 12, Remarque)
hypotheses.note: the canonical structure projOfAff (charts hemiChart ∘ ψ) AND the structure built from j itself (transportChartedSpace along j, IsPocheAff.toPocheProj_transport); they have the same maximal atlas (Ch. 1, remarque_affine_vers_projective) and pockets depend only on it (IsPocheProj.of_maximalAtlas_eq)

questions: The proof is not printed (« Remarque »). The formalized proof needs one non-obvious step: a projective chart φ̃ of a neighbourhood of a projective segment from M ∈ P, equal to j ∘ φ near M, is j ∘ χ along the whole segment for an affine chart χ (the hemisphere j(ℝⁿ) is locally constant along a connected set: eventually_eq_affineEquiv_of_isPreconnected); so projective segments from P are affine segments and condition b transfers. No reading involved.

hypotheses.note: IsCoqueProj P l φ z

hypotheses.paper: V localement projective
hypotheses.note: no HasGroupoid needed

hypotheses.paper: φ(P)‾ un corps convexe de S(n) (Ch. 1, Déf. 11)
hypotheses.note: IsCorpsConvexeS n (closure (φ '' P)), closure in S(n) (overline checked on the scan, p. 248: it covers φ(P))

questions: No proof is printed. Formalized: ⇐ a line of H̊ in φ(P) is a half-line whose closure holds s(v) and −s(v) (does not use convexity); ⇒ F(closure φ(P)) = closure F(φ(P)) − {O} (Sphere.F_closure) is convex because ±x in the closed cone would give, through an interior point, a whole line of H̊ in φ(P). Compactness is that of S(n), the interior contains the open φ(P) ≠ ∅.

kb_proposals: A segment of a manifold is a segment in EVERY compatible chart around it (IsGXSegment.image_eq; IsAffSegment.image_eq: ψ(M,N) = [ψM, ψN]; IsProjSegment.image_eq: ψ(M,N) = (ψM, ψN), ψN ≠ −ψM), and two compatible charts (or a chart and a developing map) with the same germ at one point agree along any connected set (eqOn_of_germ_eq, eqOn_of_germ_eq_isDeveloping): the tools for Chapter 2's « carte compatible d'un voisinage de (M, N) ayant en M même germe que φ » (Chapter2/Poches).

The canonical projective structure of a locally affine manifold is Benzecri.projOfAff; use `attribute [local instance] projOfAff hasGroupoid_projOfAff` in a section. A projective chart equal to j ∘ (affine chart) near one point is so along any connected set (eventually_eq_affineEquiv_of_isPreconnected); pocket predicates depend only on the maximal atlas (IsPocheProj.of_maximalAtlas_eq).

Open hemisphere H̊ (Déf. 6) vs S(n): affine segments of H̊ = segments of S(n) (Sphere.coe_image_affineSegment); Déf. 8 convexity = convexity in H̊ (Sphere.isConvexPart_iff_isAffConvex); lines of H̊ = half-lines of S(n) (isAffLine_hemi_iff); F(closure A) = closure F(A) − {O} (Sphere.F_closure); GS(E) carries closed segments to closed segments (Sphere.GSE.image_smul_closedSeg).

An open subset of ℝⁿ is a locally affine manifold through Mathlib's Opens.instChartedSpace / instHasGroupoid (gxGroupoid is ClosedUnderRestriction), and its inclusion is IsDeveloping by `rfl` (isDeveloping_val_demiDroiteOuverte): a cheap source of non-degenerate examples.
